Treatment Summary
The patient presented following a rear-end motor vehicle collision with complaints of
neck pain and stiffness. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the
injury described, and the symptom pattern is typical for a cervical strain of this
kind. Over the course of sixteen visits, care consisted of physical examination,
range-of-motion assessment, a structured therapy program, and home exercise
instruction. Physical examination identified reduced cervical range of motion and
paraspinal muscle tenderness, supporting the diagnosis, while certain neurological
screening tests returned normal results. No prior injury to the cervical region is
documented in the available history. The course of treatment followed a conventional
progression, with visit frequency decreasing as the patient's symptoms improved and
pain levels declined. Billing records reflect single entries for each service
rendered, with no duplicated charges identified. At last review, the patient was
improving and was discharged to self-directed home exercise.
